title: Continuous batching scheduler tuning experiments - batch size / timeout / fairness / tail latency
content:
Summary:
This doc records a set of continuous-batching scheduler experiments exploring the trade-offs between max_batch_size, max_wait_ms (timeout), and fairness heuristics. Goal: reduce p99 tail latency while preserving throughput and keeping average latency acceptable for interactive workloads. These are iterative, informal experiment notes - see linked artifacts for raw traces and scripts.

Context and motivation:
- Continuous batching aims to increase GPU utilization by grouping requests that arrive close in time.
- Too aggressive batching increases tail latency (p99/p99.9) for latency-sensitive requests; too conservative batching wastes GPU cycles.
- We suspect that current defaults (max_batch_size=64, max_wait_ms=12, fairness=fifo) are suboptimal for conversational workloads with bursty, short requests.

Hardware / testbed:
- Instance: 8xA100-80GB cluster, single model replica used per test to measure single-replica behavior.
- Model: 13B LLM (quantized int8 path), typical 512 token context.
- Load generator: local loadgen with poisson arrivals + synthetic mix of short/long prompt lengths (65% short ~ 32 tokens, 35% long ~ 256 tokens).
- Measurement: 60s warmup, 300s steady-state run, repeated 3 times per config. Metrics: qps, mean latency, p95, p99, p99.9, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, dispatch fairness (measured by per-request queue time distribution).

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Vary max_batch_size: [16, 32, 48, 64]
- Vary max_wait_ms: [6, 12, 24, 48]
- Fairness mode: [fifo, age-based, size-aware] (age-based prefers older requests; size-aware tries to avoid head-of-line blocking of short requests)
- Total permutations: 4 x 4 x 3 = 48 configurations; we ran prioritized subset (24) first.

Key findings (summary):
1) Small batch sizes (16/32) with short timeouts (6-12ms) produce the best p99 and p99.9 for mixed workloads, with modest qps drop (~8-12%) vs max_batch_size=64.
2) Large batches (64) with longer timeouts (24-48ms) maximize GPU throughput but p99 degraded significantly (up to 2.3x) for short requests.
3) Age-based fairness reduces tail latency for short requests in presence of long requests by ~18% p99 at similar throughput compared to fifo. Size-aware fairness improved mean latency but had edge cases that hurt throughput for some arrival mixes.
4) There is a sweet spot at max_batch_size=32, max_wait_ms=12, fairness=age-based for our canonical workload: p99 down ~28% from baseline (64/12/fifo) while qps is ~92% of baseline.

Representative raw results (median across 3 runs):
Config | qps | mean_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | p99.9_ms | GPU_util
----------------------------------------------------------------
64 / 12 / fifo  | 480 | 72  | 140 | 420 | 870  | 78%
32 / 12 / fifo  | 445 | 68  | 130 | 330 | 720  | 74%
32 / 12 / age   | 440 | 66  | 125 | 260 | 610  | 73%
16 / 6 / age    | 430 | 64  | 120 | 240 | 560  | 68%
48 / 24 / fifo  | 495 | 80  | 155 | 590 | 1160 | 82%
64 / 48 / fifo  | 510 | 98  | 220 | 930 | 1820 | 85%

Interpretation and profiling notes:
- The p99 tail is dominated by queueing delay, not execution time, when a long request sits at the head of a large batch; blocking short requests behind long ones increases observed p99.
- GPU utilization increases with batch size as expected; however, the incremental throughput gains diminish beyond batch=48 for this model due to kernel saturation.
- We captured traces showing that dispatch latency (time from enqueue to dispatch) is the bulk of p99 difference. See linked perf traces (Confluence) for flamegraphs.
- Age-based fairness implementation needs to ensure it does not constantly starve long requests - we observed throughput oscillations in some mixes when age threshold too aggressive.

Recommendations (short-term):
- Adopt conservative defaults for hosted API low-latency profiles: max_batch_size=32, max_wait_ms=12, fairness=age-based (age_threshold_ms=18). This should be the recommended profile for "interactive" workloads.
- Keep throughput-optimized profile for background/batch inference with defaults: max_batch_size=64, max_wait_ms=48, fairness=fifo.
- Add auto-profile selection heuristic: if observed median request tokens < 60 and mean interarrival < X, switch to interactive profile. (Follow-up: define X and safe hysteresis).

Implementation action items:
- [Ravi] Submit PR to add age-based scheduler variant and configuration flags (PR link in linked artifacts). Ensure unit tests for starvation/throughput regression.
- [Hannah] Add end-to-end CI perf job that runs 3 canonical workload mixes on PRs touching scheduler (low-cost sampling).
- [Tom] Instrument per-request enqueue time in traces and add dashboard showing queueing contribution to latency (p50/p95/p99 split).

Open questions / next experiments:
- Test with multi-replica routing: how interaction between smart routing and batching affects end-to-end p99 when fallback to other replicas occurs.
- Explore dynamic batch size policies (start small, grow if queue depth increases) vs static max_batch_size. Preliminary microbenchmarks suggested promise but need full-load test.
- Evaluate size-aware fairness further with more realistic customer traces (request-length distribution) - flagging for solutions-eng to share sanitized traces.

Appendix - notes on measurement stability:
- We saw config-dependent variance; runs repeated 3x and we report median. For configs where variance >10% on p99 we re-ran 5x.
- Loadgen script and raw logs are in linked artifacts; use tag "cbatch-experiments-2025-11" when referencing.

Bottom line:
For our 13B int8 path and mixed conversational workload, moving defaults toward smaller batch sizes (32) with modest timeouts (12ms) and an age-based fairness heuristic yields substantially lower p99 with limited throughput loss. Recommendation: adopt interactive profile defaults and ship age-based scheduler behind a feature flag, monitor in canary.
